chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from one of our companions, from Ibn Fazzal, from Marwan, from Abdul Malik, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who bought something from the covering of the Ka'bah. He fulfilled his need with part of it, and part remained in his hand. Is it permissible for him to sell it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He sells what he wishes, and gifts what he does not wish, and benefits from it, and seeks its blessings.' I said: 'Can the deceased be shrouded with it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No.'

key_terms.يَصْلُحُ بَيْعُهُ: Is it permissible to sell it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling or using items from the Ka'bah's covering?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the juridical status of Kiswat al-Ka'bah remnants, distinguishing between their commercial utility and ritual purity. While the Imam permits selling or gifting the fabric to retain its spiritual blessings (barakah), he explicitly prohibits using it for shrouing the dead, a ruling that reflects the scholarly consensus on the specific sanctity of the Ka'bah's covering versus general sacred items. This highlights the nuanced Shia approach to 'respect for sacred objects' (Ihtiram al-Muqaddasat) without conflating it with ritual impurity or absolute prohibition.
